requirements.title: Program entities with program-wide identity are global entities and have global identifiers
requirements.definition: Program units, common blocks, external procedures, entities with binding labels, external input/output units, pending data transfer operations, and images are global entities. The standard specifies which names, submodule identifiers, and binding labels are global identifiers.

pending.program-unit-common-external-and-binding: Source-use plan for program units, common blocks, external procedures, and binding-label entities; executable lookup facets remain under their declaration or association owner.
pending.io-pending-transfer-and-image-global-ent: Source-use plan names existing owners doc/catalogues/units_12_5_1.json for external units and doc/catalogues/id_specifier_12_6_2_9.json for pending transfers; image global-entity observations are out of scope by user decision.
pending.names-as-global-identifiers: Plan global/local collision source controls under 19.3.1 using a module or external procedure name as the global identifier.
pending.submodule-identifier-as-global: Source-use plan names existing owner doc/catalogues/submodules_14_2_3.json; no duplicate submodule syntax check is created here.
pending.binding-label-as-global: Source-use plan names existing owner doc/catalogues/bind_attribute_data_entities_8_5_5.json and the uniqueness controls in this section.

requirements.title: An entity of the program has no more than one binding label
requirements.definition: An entity of the program shall not be identified by more than one binding label.

pending.single-binding-label-per-entity: Source-control plan with one entity spelling carrying two binding-label sources and a control deleting exactly one label source; no mandatory diagnostic is claimed for this unnumbered program restriction.

requirements.title: Specified global identifiers are mutually unique, with binding labels compared case-insensitively
requirements.definition: The global identifier of an entity shall not match another global identifier, and a binding label shall not match another global entity identifier after ignoring case.

pending.distinct-global-identifiers: Source-control plan with two program global identifiers intentionally spelled alike and a one-property control renaming exactly one global; no mandatory diagnostic is claimed absent a numbered owner.
pending.case-insensitive-binding-label-distinctn: Source-control plan with BIND(C,NAME="scope_case") and BIND(C,NAME="SCOPE_CASE") on otherwise distinct entities; the control changes only one label spelling to a distinct token.

requirements.title: Processors may assign additional global identifiers to other entities
requirements.definition: A processor may assign a global identifier to an entity not specified by the standard to have a global identifier, such as an intrinsic procedure.

pending.processor-assigned-global-identifier-lat: No portable oracle can require a processor to assign such an identifier or expose its spelling; future tests must avoid depending on a particular extra external symbol.

requirements.title: Processor-assigned global identifiers must differ from all other global identifiers
requirements.definition: For a processor-assigned global identifier, the processor shall ensure that the assigned global identifier differs from all other global identifiers in the program.

pending.processor-assigned-global-identifier-dis: No portable oracle can observe every processor-assigned global identifier. Source-use plan keeps user-specified global identifiers distinct and forbids fixture assumptions about hidden symbols.
